'''Columbia Gas Transmission''' is an operating system of natural gas pipelines in the United States.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2kQCnMC Columbia Gas Transmission,] Wikipedia, accessed Aug. 25, 2021.</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from points in the Midwest and Southeast to New York.<ref name=source1/>

==Background==

=== Main Line ===
Columbia Gas Transmission is owned and operated by TC Energy.<ref>[https://www.transcanada.com/en/operations/natural-gas/columbia-gas-transmission/ Columbia Gas Transmission] Transcanada, accessed Dec. 2017</ref> It was acquired by TC Energy as part of its $13 billion purchase of the Columbia Pipeline group in 2016.<ref>[http://www.dispatch.com/article/20160317/NEWS/303179760 Columbia Pipeline Group sold to Canadian firm in $13 billion deal] ''Columbus Dispatch,'' Mar. 17, 2016</ref> The acquisition came after TC Energy's 2015 failure to win approval for its proposed Keystone XL Pipeline, and TC Energy's CEO Russ Girling stressed the company's desire to increase its capacity to carry gas from the lucrative Marcellus and Utica Shale regions.<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2016/03/17/columbia-pipeline-group-transcanada-sale/81929578/ Keystone Pipeline company TransCanada acquires Columbia Pipeline] USA Today, Mar. 17, 2016, accessed Aug. 25, 2021.</ref>

In July 2023, a section of the pipeline in western Virginia exploded, prompting a temporary localized shutdown.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pilotonline.com/2023/07/25/gas-pipeline-explodes-near-interstate-in-rural-virginia-no-injuries-reported|title=https://www.pilotonline.com/2023/07/25/gas-pipeline-explodes-near-interstate-in-rural-virginia-no-injuries-reported|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In July 2023, TC Energy announced that it will divest a 40% interest in its Columbia Gas Transmission and Columbia Gulf Transmission pipelines for US$5.2 billion to Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP). The transaction is expected to close in fourth quarter 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/tc-energy-sell-40-interest-columbia-gas-columbia-gulf-pipelines-c52-bln-2023-07-24/?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email|title=TC Energy to sell 40% in Columbia gas transmission systems for $4 billion|work=Reuters|access-date=2023-09-08|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lngglobal.com/tc-energy-to-sell-40-interest-in-columbia-gas-and-columbia-gulf-pipelines|title=TC Energy to sell 40% interest in Columbia Gas and Columbia Gulf pipelines|last=|first=|date=24 July, 2023|website=LNG Global|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=08 September, 2023}}</ref>
===East Lateral Xpress Project===
The expansion will provide additional transportation services on Columbia Gulf’s East Lateral from Columbia Gulf’s Onshore Pool (CGT-Rayne) and the Venice Meter Station to a new delivery point with the [[Gator Express Gas Pipeline]] in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana.<ref name=eiajul21/>

As of September 2020, developers had already applied for project approval with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).<ref name=eiajul21/>

It was completed in 2025.<ref name="eiajul21" />
===Marysville Connector Pipeline===
Proposed in 2019, the expansion would supply additional gas to the Marysville, Ohio area by running a line from Dublin, Ohio to Marysville, Ohio. Developers received project approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in August 2020.<ref name=eiajul21>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas, Pipeline Projects], Energy Information Administration, Jun. 7, 2021, accessed Jul. 12, 2021</ref>

Facing legal issues over land rights, Columbia Gas requested a 3 year extension to the approval expiration date, which would have been August 2023. The request was granted in June 2023.<ref name=":1" />

No update on the project has been released since, and it is considered shelved as of 2025.
===Virginia Expansion Project===
The expansion project is in Virginia. It is a capacity expansion only, with no additional kilometers added.<ref name=eia>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects] Energy Information Agency, Jul. 21, 2020, accessed Aug. 25, 2021.</ref>
===Louisiana XPress Expansion Project===
Columbia Gulf Transmission applied for an expansion in 2019 called the Louisiana XPress Project. The expansion would cost US$472 million and add 493 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) of natural gas transportation capacity. The expansion would effect Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, and Louisiana. It does not include adding any additional miles of pipeline.<ref name=eia/>

In August 2020 it was reported that Columbia Gulf Transmission was pressing the U.S. Federal Energy Regulator Commission (FERC) to fast-track authorization of the Louisiana XPress Project which already received a favorable environmental assessment from FERC in February 2020. The promoters of the project, which will mainly provide additional supply into Cheniere Energy’s operating [[Sabine Pass LNG Terminal]] in Louisiana's Cameron Parish, are pushing to begin construction of the project in September 2020 to avoid the rainy season in order to meet their intended February 2022 in-service target date.<ref>[https://www.1012industryreport.com/pipelines/the-louisiana-xpress-tries-to-fast-track-project-to-sabine-pass/ The Louisiana XPress: CGT wants to fast-track project to Sabine Pass], 1012 Industry Report, Aug. 18, 2020, accessed Aug. 25, 2021.</ref>

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project was under-construction.<ref name=eiaapr21>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php U.S. natural gas pipeline projects], U.S. Energy Information Administration, Apr. 29, 2021, accessed Aug. 25, 2021.</ref> As of January 2022, part of the project was complete<ref name="eiaapr21" />, but the TC Energy website still identified the project as in development.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/virginia-electrification-project/|title=Virginia Electrification Project|website=www.tcenergy.com|language=en|access-date=2022-10-06}}</ref>
=== Virginia Electrification Project ===
The Virginia Electrification Project involves the modification of various compressor stations to increase capacity to Columbia Gas Transmission LLC's Market Area 33 and Market Area 34 in southeast Virginia, United States.

=== Northern Loop Project ===
The Northern Loop Project involves abandoning in-place pipeline and replacing a 14-mile segment in Ohio, according to a mapped route available in the application materials on the developer's website.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.columbiagasohio.com/services/work-in-your-neighborhood/northern-loop-project|title=Northern Loop Pipeline Project - Columbia Gas of Ohio|website=www.columbiagasohio.com|access-date=2025-10-14}}</ref> The EIA notes the route would also run in Pennsylvania, but there is no evidence for this elsewhere.<ref name="eiaapr21" /> The project is considered to be shelved as of 2025.<ref name="eiaapr21" />

=== Eastern Panhandle Expansion Project ===
This expansion project is part of the [[Mountaineer Gas Pipeline]].

=== Mainline 100 and Mainline 200 Replacement Project ===
This involves replacement of lines serving the area south of the Means Measuring station in Kentucky, United States, which has experienced increased population density.
